claims.assertion: Static application security testing (SAST) linters and high-entropy secret scanners fulfill mutually exclusive security boundaries; linters detect dangerous AST API patterns and insecure cryptography, while secret scanners calculate Shannon entropy and regex token shapes.
claims.source: Umair Mirza: 'How to Catch Security Vulnerabilities in Code Before They Reach Your Pull Requests' (freeCodeCamp, Sept 2026)

claims.assertion: Pre-commit passes all staged files as trailing arguments, whereas Microsoft CST DevSkim CLI only accepts a single target path via -I; multi-file commits break unless mediated by an execution loop dispatcher.
claims.source: Umair Mirza: 'Create a Pre-Commit Configuration' (2026) + DevSkim CLI Specification

claims.assertion: Security guardrails cannot be trusted based on successful installations alone; hooks must be empirically verified via deliberate synthetic failure smoke tests (MD5 weak hash and high-entropy dummy key) asserting non-zero exit codes (Exit 1).
claims.source: Umair Mirza: 'Verify the Setup With a Deliberate Failure' (2026)

claims.assertion: Developer workstations cannot provide authoritative security guarantees because pre-commit hooks can be bypassed using git commit --no-verify; remote CI must enforce identical checks with full git history depth (fetch-depth: 0) and upload SARIF reports to the repository security tab.
claims.source: Umair Mirza: 'Add Security Checks to CI Too' (2026) + GitHub SARIF Security Governance
